cards.title: Test one variable at a time and watch real behavior with heat maps
cards.summary: Run simple A/B tests on single elements and use heat maps to see where visitors click, scroll and ignore.
cards.use_when: You want to improve conversion scientifically rather than guessing, and need to prioritize which element to change first.

cards.title: Keep a weekly marketing routine of one email, your post goal, one data-driven change
cards.summary: A simple repeating checklist prevents burnout and builds momentum: send an email, hit your social goal, check the dashboard, adjust one thing.
cards.use_when: You're managing marketing alongside everything else and need a sustainable weekly cadence rather than launching five strategies at once.

cards.title: Use Sidekick across setup, analysis and creative tasks
cards.summary: Route recurring store questions and tasks — attribution advice, menu audits, app auditing, copy, segments and campaigns — through Sidekick instead of digging through admin manually.
cards.use_when: You need a quick answer or action in Shopify admin without knowing where to click, or you want to move faster on setup, optimization and content.

cards.title: Optimize WordPress permalinks and strip default plugins after install
cards.summary: Configure clean post-name URLs and deactivate bundled plugins before building a WooCommerce store, so product URLs stay readable and the site isn't bloated.
cards.use_when: You've just installed WordPress and WooCommerce on your host and need to lock down URL structure and plugin bloat before adding products.

cards.title: Set origin-based vs destination-based tax correctly per state
cards.summary: Cross-reference TaxJar to determine whether each state taxes by shop base address or customer shipping address, then enter rates with four decimal places in WooCommerce.
cards.use_when: You're configuring WooCommerce tax rates and need to decide which address WooCommerce should use as the tax basis for each state you sell into.

cards.title: Charge flat-rate shipping per item instead of per order
cards.summary: Use the [qty] shortcode in WooCommerce's flat-rate cost field to multiply a dollar amount by the number of items in the cart.
cards.use_when: You want shipping priced per unit (e.g., heavy or bulky goods) rather than a flat charge for the whole order.

cards.title: Install Stripe and PayPal via dedicated third-party plugins, not defaults
cards.summary: The source recommends skipping WooCommerce's bundled payment plugins and installing 'Payment Plugins for Stripe WooCommerce' and 'Payment Plugins for PayPal WooCommerce' for API-key setup.
cards.use_when: You're connecting card and PayPal payments and deciding which gateway plugin to install and how to enter API credentials.

cards.title: Create global product attributes before building variable products
cards.summary: For variable products, define attributes globally first, then attach them to the product and generate variations with individual SKUs, images, prices and stock.
cards.use_when: You're creating a variable product (e.g., apparel with sizes and colors) and need a repeatable, correctly ordered workflow.

cards.title: Build a Variable Product with Global Attributes
cards.summary: Correct order of operations for creating purchasable WooCommerce variable products with global attributes and generated variations.
cards.use_when: Adding a product to the catalog that comes in multiple sizes, weights, colors or option types and must be purchasable per variation.

cards.title: Install Payment Gateways for Stripe and PayPal
cards.summary: Skip default payment plugins and wire dedicated Stripe/PayPal gateway plugins so customers can pay on-site without third-party redirects.
cards.use_when: Preparing a store checkout to accept card and PayPal payments directly on your own domain instead of sending buyers off-site.

cards.title: Set Store Address, Selling and Shipping Locations
cards.summary: Configure WooCommerce General settings so tax, currency and shipping only apply to the markets you actually serve.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restricting which countries and regions your store sells and ships to before launching products.

cards.title: Set a Catalog Placeholder Image
cards.summary: Upload a branded placeholder image so products with missing or broken images still look intentional in the shop grid.
cards.use_when: Launching a shop catalog where image uploads may fail or products may lack images, and you do not want empty grey boxes in the grid.

cards.title: Choose Tax-Inclusive or Tax-Exclusive Product Pricing
cards.summary: Decide whether your entered product prices include tax, since this changes what shoppers see on the shop page versus checkout.
cards.use_when: Configuring store tax settings before entering product prices, especially for multi-state or multi-country tax rules.

cards.title: Build Location-Based Tax Rates with State Rows
cards.summary: Create per-state tax rules so US customers are charged the correct rate for where they are, with a country-level fallback.
cards.use_when: Selling into the US (or any region with sub-region tax rates) and needing checkout to apply the right percentage automatically.

cards.title: Set Weight and Dimension Units Before Adding Products
cards.summary: Choose store-wide weight and dimension units early so product data and shipping calculations are entered consistently.
cards.use_when: Configuring a store that ships physical goods and will rely on weight/dimension data for shipping rates.

cards.title: Enable Customer Registration with Subscriber Role
cards.summary: Allow shoppers to create accounts on the store while keeping their permissions limited to subscriber level.
cards.use_when: Setting up account-based features such as order history, saved addresses, wishlists and logged-in checkout.

cards.title: Set Post Name Permalinks for Clean Product and Page URLs
cards.summary: Switch WordPress permalinks to post name so shop, product and post URLs are readable for shoppers and search engines.
cards.use_when: Immediately after installing WordPress and before creating shop, product or blog pages that should rank and be shareable.

cards.title: Configure Site Title and Tagline as Positioning Statements
cards.summary: Use the WordPress site title and tagline to state clearly what the store sells and where, instead of leaving a generic name.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new store and choosing the wording that appears in the browser tab, search results and site header.

cards.title: Choose a Lightweight Ecommerce Theme and Build with a Page Builder
cards.summary: Use a lightweight WooCommerce-supporting theme plus a page builder instead of a heavy pre-designed theme for full design control.
cards.use_when: Deciding the design stack for a new storefront before you build the homepage, shop and product pages.

cards.title: Back Up and Clean a Fresh WordPress Install
cards.summary: Remove default plugins and dashboard clutter and confirm backups exist before building the store.
cards.use_when: Right after installing WordPress and before installing store plugins, to start from a clean, secure base.

cards.title: Verify Hosting, Domain and SSL Before Building
cards.summary: Claim the domain, verify email and enable HTTPS so checkout runs on a secure, controllable foundation.
cards.use_when: Commissioning hosting and the domain for a new store, prior to installing WordPress and WooCommerce.

cards.title: Build Store Front-End Structure That Mirrors Top Ecommerce Sites
cards.summary: Lay out the storefront with the standard components shoppers expect on the homepage, shop and product pages.
cards.use_when: Planning homepage and shop-page sections for a new store, so shoppers can search, browse and buy without friction.

cards.title: Set State and Country Tax Rates with Priority Rules
cards.summary: Create WooCommerce tax rate rows for specific states, whole countries and fallback rates, then use priority numbers to resolve overlapping rules.
cards.use_when: Configuring tax tables for a store that ships to multiple US states or countries and you need correct rates at checkout.

cards.title: Use Shipping Zones to Localize Fulfillment Offers
cards.summary: WooCommerce shipping zones let you scope free-shipping and flat-rate rules to a country or a single state.
cards.use_when: Deciding what shipping to offer for a whole country versus a specific state or region, and wanting region-specific perks.

cards.title: Choose Per-Order or Per-Item Flat Rate Shipping
cards.summary: Flat-rate shipping can be charged once per order or multiplied by quantity using a formula, and heavy goods usually need the per-item version.
cards.use_when: Setting the delivery cost for a physical product line where shipping multiple units would otherwise be unprofitable.

cards.title: Create Shipping Classes for Heavy or Premium Packaging
cards.summary: Shipping classes let one zone charge a different rate for special packaging while keeping a normal default cost for everything else.
cards.use_when: Storing products whose packaging weight or cost differs materially from the standard packaging, e.g. premium or heavy packs.

cards.title: Enable Cod and Verify Stripe and PayPal Setup
cards.summary: Add cash on delivery plus Stripe and PayPal so customers can pay on-site, and test connections before switching to live.
cards.use_when: Turning on payment methods in a new store and connecting gateway accounts safely.

cards.title: Configure Accounts and Checkout Login Options
cards.summary: Guest checkout plus optional account creation reduces checkout friction while still building a customer list.
cards.use_when: Setting account and checkout behaviour for a new store to balance frictionless purchase against account-based retention.

cards.title: Turn On Transactional Email Notifications Per Event
cards.summary: WooCommerce emails are per-event and many are off by default, so enable and edit each one you actually want sent.
cards.use_when: After orders start flowing, when customers report missing confirmations or you want branded status emails.

cards.title: Keep the Store in Coming Soon Until Catalogs and Pages Are Ready
cards.summary: Site visibility is a launch switch; keep the store hidden while building, then go live deliberately.
cards.use_when: Building a store before launch and deciding when customers should be able to reach it.

cards.title: Fill Store Details and Page Assignments in Settings
cards.summary: Store name, address, policies and page assignments power invoices, emails and checkout links, so set them rather than relying on placeholders.
cards.use_when: Finalizing store identity and confirming the cart, checkout, account and policy pages WooCommerce uses.

cards.title: Create a Simple Physical Product With Pricing, SKU and Stock
cards.summary: The simple product flow covers name, description, price/sale price, SKU, stock, shipping dimensions and categories.
cards.use_when: Adding standard physical products to the catalog at initial setup.

cards.title: Build Variable Products from Global Attributes
cards.summary: Create attributes once at the global level, then generate all variation combinations and price each one individually.
cards.use_when: Selling a product in multiple sizes, weights or bundle options where price and stock differ per option.

cards.title: Create Virtual Downloadable Products for Digital Goods
cards.summary: Marking a product virtual removes shipping; making it downloadable attaches files customers receive after purchase.
cards.use_when: Selling ebooks, guides, templates or other digital files in the store.

cards.title: List Affiliate Products as External Products
cards.summary: External/affiliate product type sends buyers to a partner URL with custom button text while keeping the listing on your store.
cards.use_when: Monetizing affiliate programs by merchandising partner goods without fulfillment responsibility.

cards.title: Use Upsells and Cross-Sells to Raise Cart Value
cards.summary: Upsells appear as upgrade suggestions on the product/cart, while cross-sells appear as complementary recommendations.
cards.use_when: Configuring related-product recommendations on product pages and in the cart.

cards.title: Configure Coupon Type, Restrictions and Usage Limits
cards.summary: Coupons combine a discount type with spend thresholds, product/category restrictions and per-user or per-coupon caps.
cards.use_when: Running a promotional discount and controlling who can use it, on what, and how often.

cards.title: Run an End-to-End Purchase and Order Management Test
cards.summary: Testing the full buyer journey and then processing the order from admin verifies setup before launch.
cards.use_when: Before going live, and whenever payments, tax, shipping or emails change.

cards.title: Set a Static Homepage Before Building the Storefront
cards.summary: WordPress serves posts on the root URL by default; assigning a static page makes your designed homepage reachable at the domain.
cards.use_when: After creating the homepage page and before designing it in a page builder.

cards.title: Know Free Page Builder Versus Pro Widget Boundaries
cards.summary: Elementor's free widgets cover layout, headings, images, text, video and buttons, while advanced widgets such as posts, portfolio, loop and carousel require the pro tier or add-on plugins.
cards.use_when: Planning how to build product and homepage sections without buying pro, and deciding whether add-on widget plugins are needed.

cards.title: Build a WooCommerce Homepage Banner in Elementor with Containers
cards.summary: Step-by-step Elementor container setup for a conversion-focused store homepage banner with heading, CTA button, and social proof counter.
cards.use_when: Building or rebuilding the hero/banner section of a WooCommerce storefront homepage in Elementor, or deciding how to structure the top-of-page offer area.

cards.title: Roll Back Elementor to a Stable Version Before Building
cards.summary: Safely freeze a page builder at a known stable release via Elementor's version control to avoid mid-build incompatibilities.
cards.use_when: Before starting or resuming a storefront build when a page builder has just released a major version and layouts, widgets, or third-party add-ons may break.

cards.title: Speed Up Store Builds with Elementor Global Colors and Global Fonts
cards.summary: Configure global brand colours, fonts, container width, and zero default padding/gaps once so every new section inherits the store's design system.
cards.use_when: When first configuring a WooCommerce theme/page builder so that every subsequent product section, category block, or landing page is faster to build and visually consistent.

cards.title: Use Position Absolute + Offsets to Place Decorative Store Images Precisely
cards.summary: Take hero and section images out of normal flow with absolute positioning and numeric offsets for pixel-accurate layering.
cards.use_when: Layering product photos, badges, paw prints, or accent graphics over a hero, category block, or promo box where images must overlap copy or each other at exact coordinates.

cards.title: Embed Best-Selling and Latest WooCommerce Products via Shortcode
cards.summary: Pull live WooCommerce product collections into builder sections using the official WooCommerce product shortcodes.
cards.use_when: Adding a best-sellers or new-arrivals rail to a homepage, landing page, or category page without hand-picking products that go stale.

cards.title: Import a Prebuilt Elementor Template (e.g. Reviews Section) Instead of Building From Scratch
cards.summary: Upload a saved Elementor JSON template and insert it as a section, then customize its widgets rather than reconstructing the layout.
cards.use_when: Adding a common but tedious store section such as testimonials/reviews, contact, or FAQ where you already have a saved design file.

cards.title: Build a Countdown-Timer Promo Box for Offers and Drops
cards.summary: Set up a styled countdown widget inside a promo box to create urgency for a sale, launch, or limited drop.
cards.use_when: Running a time-limited promotion, flash sale, or product drop on a homepage or campaign landing page where urgency is part of the offer.

cards.title: Build a Category Showcase Section with Floating Badges
cards.summary: Lay out category tiles as clickable images with overlaid, rounded category-name badges that double as navigation.
cards.use_when: Building a homepage or landing page category block that routes shoppers into top-level product categories (e.g. dog food, cat food).

cards.title: Make Elementor Store Sections Responsive Without Breaking Desktop
cards.summary: Fix tablets and mobile using per-breakpoint container widths, reduced typography, per-breakpoint padding, and Order instead of physically moving elements.
cards.use_when: After building a desktop store homepage/section, when it breaks on tablet or mobile and you need to correct it without regressing the desktop layout.

cards.title: Set a Global Page Background and Full-Width Layout Once Per Page
cards.summary: Use Page Settings to apply a single background colour and full-width canvas instead of styling every section individually.
cards.use_when: When a store homepage or landing page needs a consistent background and its sections must span the full browser width.

cards.title: Use Negatives Margins and Order to Control Store Section Spacing
cards.summary: Fine-tune spacing between hero copy, buttons, and grouped elements with margins, negative margins, and container order rather than adding empty blocks.
cards.use_when: Tightening or separating elements within a product hero, promo box, or footer strip where default gaps look wrong.

cards.title: Create Global Font and Colour Shortcuts Inside Widget Settings
cards.summary: Save frequently used fonts and colours as named global presets from within any typography/colour picker to avoid re-selecting them repeatedly.
cards.use_when: When building a store page and you find yourself re-applying the same font family, size/weight combination, or brand colour on every heading and button.

cards.title: Plan for a Blog Section by Deferring Styling Until Posts Exist
cards.summary: Add the blog/latest-posts block to the homepage structurally, but wait to style it until real blog content exists so the design preview isn't misleading.
cards.use_when: Building a store homepage in a builder where a blog/news section is planned but no real posts have been published yet.

cards.title: Fix the SVG Icon Upload 'Only One Image Shows' Bug
cards.summary: Recover missing SVG icons in the media library by publishing and refreshing the editor, then re-opening the uploader.
cards.use_when: When uploading a batch of SVG icons (for store badges, payment icons, CTA arrows) and only one appears in the media library.

cards.title: Renaming and the Structure Panel Keep Complex Store Builds Sane
cards.summary: Double-click to rename containers and use the Structure tree to navigate, select, and reorder deeply nested store sections.
cards.use_when: Managing a multi-section store homepage where containers are nested several levels deep and selecting the right one in the canvas is slow or error-prone.

cards.title: Choose the Right Text Widget for Store Copy
cards.summary: Use Heading for large display text and Text Editor for paragraphs, because they offer different styling control.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to add hero headlines, product descriptions, or mixed-format body copy to a store page in a visual builder.

cards.title: Building a responsive homepage in Elementor (tablet/mobile pass)
cards.summary: Method for making an Elementor page builder homepage banner, product and category sections responsive across tablet and mobile by adjusting padding, direction, width and gaps.
cards.use_when: You are laying out a WooCommerce store homepage in Elementor and it looks broken on tablet or mobile breakpoints.

cards.title: Adding more pages before theme customization
cards.summary: Create a contact page and a blog list page as standalone WordPress pages, then finish them alongside theme customization so site-wide settings apply everywhere.
cards.use_when: You have published a store homepage and now need additional pages such as contact and blog before doing global theme setup.

cards.title: Designing a contact page banner and contact-detail cards
cards.summary: Create a styled contact page top banner and reusable contact-detail cards (phone, email, address) using containers and icon widgets.
cards.use_when: You are building or polishing the contact page of a WooCommerce store and want it visually consistent with the brand.

cards.title: Building a contact form with MetForm in Elementor
cards.summary: Assemble a styled contact form (name, email, message, submit) using the MetForm widget, then wire admin notifications.
cards.use_when: Your store contact page needs a functional form that emails submissions to you.

cards.title: Embedding a store location map widget
cards.summary: Add a Google Maps widget focused on your shop location by feeding the map the exact place title plus store name.
cards.use_when: Your store's contact page or footer should show where customers can find you physically.

cards.title: Writing and publishing store blog posts
cards.summary: Create blog posts in the WordPress block/rich-text editor with featured image, categories and tags, then surface them via a dedicated posts page.
cards.use_when: You want content marketing or SEO articles attached to your store and discoverable by visitors.

cards.title: Configuring the blog post widget on the homepage
cards.summary: Style the Elementor blog-posts widget into a clean grid of image, metadata and title for a storefront homepage blog section.
cards.use_when: You want to surface recent articles on the homepage and control exactly what each card shows.

cards.title: Setting site identity: logo, title, tagline and favicon
cards.summary: Configure WordPress site identity so the header logo, browser tab icon, site title and tagline reflect the store brand.
cards.use_when: You are doing the global brand pass on a new store and the header still shows a default site title instead of a logo.

cards.title: Setting global theme layout, colors and scroll-to-top
cards.summary: Use the theme customizer's Layout and Colors panels to set a site-wide background, container width, header color, footer columns, copyright text and scroll-to-top button.
cards.use_when: You want store-wide consistency instead of fixing colors and spacing page by page.

cards.title: Configuring WooCommerce catalog and product display settings
cards.summary: Tune the WooCommerce customizer panels so shop pages show the right number of products, consistent image sizes, hover behavior, sale tags and add-to-cart style.
cards.use_when: You are finishing the shop archive and need catalog, image and product-card behavior set up correctly.

cards.title: Creating header and footer nav menus in WordPress
cards.summary: Build the primary header menu and multiple footer menus so visitors can actually navigate the store.
cards.use_when: Your store pages are published but there is no working navigation in the header or footer.

cards.title: Building footer widget columns with logo, menus and contact info
cards.summary: Populate theme footer widget areas with a logo block, descriptive text, navigation menu blocks and contact details.
cards.use_when: The footer area is empty and you want quick links, brand identity and contact details there.

cards.title: Catching left-over homepage sections and finishing the pass
cards.summary: Recognize which homepage sections (e.g. blog grid, product grids) remain incomplete and defer them until their dependent content or global setup exists.
cards.use_when: You are finishing a store homepage and some sections look broken or empty.

cards.title: Build a multi-column footer with navigation menus and contact details
cards.summary: Assemble a four-column footer (logo/description, quick links, website links, contact info) in a block-based theme editor, then fix column layout problems.
cards.use_when: Setting up or fixing a store footer in a block-based theme (e.g., WooCommerce block theme) so navigation, contact details and copyright display correctly.

cards.title: Apply a curated custom-CSS set to polish theme design elements
cards.summary: Use a provided sequence of custom CSS snippets (buttons, headings, counters, product cards, blog images, cart/checkout) to unify a store's visuals beyond default theme styling.
cards.use_when: When default theme styling makes product grids, buttons, counters, blog images or cart/checkout pages look unpolished and you want consistent store-wide design quickly.

cards.title: Replace default cart and checkout widgets with WooCommerce shortcodes
cards.summary: Swap bloated default cart/checkout widget layouts for WooCommerce shortcodes to get cleaner, theme-matching cart and checkout pages.
cards.use_when: When cart or checkout pages use default template/widget layouts that look inconsistent with the rest of the store, and you want a simpler page structure.

cards.title: Enable and style a page header banner with breadcrumbs
cards.summary: Turn on the theme's Page Header template part to add a branded title banner with breadcrumbs to shop, blog, cart and other pages.
cards.use_when: When non-homepage store pages (shop, blog, cart, contact) start abruptly with no header context and you want a consistent branded banner with breadcrumbs.

cards.title: Change the blog author display name store-wide
cards.summary: Edit the WordPress user profile so blog posts show a chosen full display name instead of a username.
cards.use_when: When blog posts on the store's content section show a generic or blank author name and you want a personal or brand author name to appear.

cards.title: Verify storefront pages end-to-end after setup
cards.summary: Run a structured walkthrough of all key storefront pages (shop, product, blog, contact, account, cart) after design and configuration to confirm functionality and appearance.
cards.use_when: After completing theme setup, CSS, footer and shortcode work, before handing off or launching an ecommerce store.

cards.title: WooCommerce Setup Order: From Blank to Sellable Store
cards.summary: A sequenced checklist for standing up a WooCommerce store: domain, WordPress, theme and builder, payments, shipping, taxes, then products.
cards.use_when: You are launching a new WooCommerce store from nothing and need the correct build order so later steps (payments, shipping, taxes) have products and addresses to bind to.

cards.title: Installing and Importing a Blocksy + Elementor Starter Site
cards.summary: Click path to get Blocksy theme, Blocksy Companion, and an Elementor-built starter template onto a fresh WordPress install.
cards.use_when: You are on a fresh WordPress install and want a styled, editable storefront skeleton without designing every page from scratch.

cards.title: Creating a Simple Product in WooCommerce
cards.summary: The field-by-field path for adding a single-option product: pricing, inventory, shipping dimensions, category and image.
cards.use_when: You are listing a product with no size/color variants and need it purchasable, stocked correctly, and shipping-ready.

cards.title: Creating a Variable Product with Attributes and Generated Variations
cards.summary: How to build size/color variants in WooCommerce using an attribute list, then generate each combination and price it individually.
cards.use_when: You sell a product in multiple sizes, colors or materials and need each combination to have its own SKU, stock and price.

cards.title: Connecting Stripe and PayPal via Payment Plugins
cards.summary: Install the Stripe/PayPal WooCommerce plugins, link accounts by API, run the connection test, and stay in test mode until verified.
cards.use_when: You are turning on card and wallet payments for a WooCommerce store and want to confirm the connection before taking real money.
